Un jeu parfait pour toutes les personnes nostalgiques de ces jeux emblématiques qui ont marqué notre générations. Et ce en montrant une pléthore de genre divers (shoot them all, beat them up, tactical rpg, enigmes du professeur Layton, plates formes à la super Mario, infiltration à la solid snake, puzzle game).
Et si ne n'était que ça, le jeu regorge d'humour et de référence en tout genre (dragon ball, métroid, la reine des neiges... oui même la reine des neiges !)
Des quêtes annexes avec le game of cards bigrement addictif
Un 100% pas du tout frustrant à réaliser...
Certains peuvent critiquer que le jeu reste bon sans exceller dans aucun des domaines, mais c'est normal. Chaque genre est ici représenté pour rendre lui hommage... et ce n'est pas un jeu à remettre à un fan d'un certain genre qui voudra le tester uniquement pour le genre qu'il aime.
Bref, j'avais bien aimé le tout premier Evoland qui nous offrait une véritable expérience sur l'évolution du jeu vidéo, ici dans Evoland 2, le titre est sublimé.
Si j'avais été développeur, j'aurais créé un jeu comme celui-là !

The first [i]Evoland[/i] was a gimmick-based game.  As you move through the game, the graphics update from very primitive 2D to pretty good 3D; while the gameplay is a mishmash of different genres.  I liked it, don't get me wrong, but it's fairly shallow, especially narratively.  For the sequel, the developers took the idea of using historical graphical styles to represent different periods of in-game history, and converted that to a very solid and varied RPG with a deep and non-linear story.

Most of this game is an action hack-n-slash, be it in isometric 3D, top-down 2D, or side-on platformer.  However, there are also many, many sections which change it up, with a much wider variety than in the previous game.  Match-three, bullet hell, party-based ATB systems, puzzles, one-on-one fighter, beat-em-up... they're all there and more.  This is both a strength and a weakness.  On the one hand, it keeps things fresh and never stagnant.  But the negative is that you need pretty diverse tastes or you'll eventually hit something you don't like, or don't think is well implemented.

But it's the game's story that I find most interesting.  I don't want to go into too much detail to avoid spoilers.  But, despite starting with the cliche of the hero waking up with amnesia, the game goes on to tell a complex and non-linear story with ambiguous motivations and conclusions.  A lot of stuff is left implicit, which I mean here as a positive: this rewards paying attention and also interpretation.  The characters also all have distinct and well-realised personalities; I liked how a particular romantic relationship was clear, despite I think no romantic language being used.

Imaginative and inventive, [i]Evoland 2[/i] is great.

游戏玩完之后甚至记不得哪一段经历特别有意思，只有被反复折磨的痛苦，卸载过两次，实在是气不过才通关的。好评只是念在已经是十几年前的游戏了，不能太苛求，可能当时制作水平只能到这个程度，从现在看没有玩的必要。在这个基础上好好改造能做成很不错的游戏，可惜没有机会了。鸡肋。

I recommend this game with caution. The story is fun, the characters are great, the concept is intriguing, and there are lots of little moments that fans of just about every genre will enjoy. This game was made by geeks and nerds for geeks and nerds.

HOWEVER, the gameplay peaks at 2005 Nintendo. The only evolution is the graphics, as there is no real difference in combat or travel between any of the three eras you visit, and there definitely came a point where I wasn't playing because it was fun, but because I had put thirty hours into the game, I might as well finish it. Which, honestly, didn't give me a sense of accomplishment, but more of a sense of exhausted relief like I had finished deep cleaning my apartment before guests arrived.

The challenges and boss fights rely heavily (almost exclusively) on arcade and rouge-like style gameplay, which I generally am not a fan of. Some of the moments, both in combat and in story, toe the line between "homage" and "blatant ripoff", and it's very difficult to play without a controller.

There are some fun mini games that distract from the main plot like a CCG and some hidden gems I won't spoil, and having 30+ hours of gameplay makes it worth the money, but make sure you know what you're getting into first.

I really didn’t enjoy this game. Constantly going back and forth was annoying, and a lot of the mechanics just weren’t intuitive. The game doesn’t reward curiosity, and it tries to mix a bunch of different genres but fails at almost all of them. Combat was basically non-existent, and the controls felt clunky - I almost quit during the Street Fighter style section.

There were also game breaking visual bugs. (Tip: don’t mess with the custom settings just stick with the presets) I only finished the game out of sheer stubbornness. Some of the puzzles were okay, but most were hit or miss. The first turn-based role-playing part was especially disappointing. It was repetitive, shallow, and basically just button-mashing.

The world felt lifeless. NPCs wandered around in towns but had dull, meaningless dialogue, and there were no side quests or any real incentive to explore. Out of all the genres they experimented with, the only ones I enjoyed were the Candy Crush style mini games and the turn based combat  but it took me 10 hours just to get to that part, and the fun only lasted a couple of hours.

I kept hoping the game would eventually get good, but aside from those two segments, it was a total waste of time. Add in the performance and optimization issues, and I honestly can’t recommend this game to anyone.

As many others have said, I wish Steam had a "meh" rating. Evoland II starts off interesting, but has very little to actually call its own - its main two gimmicks are the changing art styles and its mash-up of genres. The art is well made (if generic) and it IS a neat concept, but it doesn't have any of the same puzzle elements that the original Evoland had, it just changes depending on what time period you're in. 

The genre-mashing is interesting in concept but irritating in practice. Don't like top-down shooters? Too bad, slog through 9 waves of it. Hate endless runners or platformers? Too bad, we're side-scrolling now and there's no skipping. These changes don't really add anything beyond the novelty of changing genres and references to other games, which leads into...

Whether or not you enjoy Evoland II mostly comes down to how much you enjoy references to other, more famous games. If you do, you're going to love this game because that's like 80% of its "humour" and "wit" - I enjoy a clever, well-placed reference, but when your entire game is references, it just leaves me wondering why I should play this one instead of one of the others it's reminding me of. Item descriptions about not using an important item as a bowling ball? Dialogue about a green-clad kid traumatising chickens by using them to fly? There's a creeper in the mines? This isn't clever, it's just "lol we put that famous thing into our game" and "lol isn't it funny that player behaviour is silly if you don't suspend your disbelief". The game is trying to have its cake and eat it too by asking players to take its story seriously while also repeatedly saying "did we mention this is a game? Evoland 2 é um jogo indie desenvolvido e publicado pela Shiro Games, lançado em Agosto de 2015, sendo um sucessor para o jogo de mesmo nome.
O jogo mostra a história de Kuro, ou seja lá qual for o nome atribuído ao personagem, em uma clássica aventura de RPG através das eras dos videogames.

Prós:
[list] 
[*]Evolução dos conceitos introduzidos anteriormente em conjunto à adição de novos, o principal foco do jogo, que é um visual e uma jogabilidade variadas de acordo com o tempo, é resgatado e incluído dentro da narrativa dessa vez, os estilos de jogos e desafios são expandidos e abrangem os mais diversos tipos.
[*]Variabilidade na jogabilidade permite criar situações únicas para cada cenário, além de permitir uma jogabilidade menos cansativa a abordagem feita pelos desenvolvedores traz uma experiência bem diferente do habitual, com principal sendo o clássico RPG, temos partes representando jogos de luta, estratégia, plataforma entre outros.
[*]Mapa aberto, dividido em várias seções com ótimas ambientações, e a presença de itens colecionáveis contribuindo para que a exploração seja recompensada. 
[/list]

Contras:
[list]
[*]Início lento da narrativa que demora um pouco para ficar interessante.
[*]Alta quantidade de diálogos que acabam por não levar a nenhum ponto relevante para o desenvolvimento dos personagens e suas relações e deixam o jogo cansativo em certas partes.
[/list]

Evoland 2 é uma excelente sequência com uma gigantesca evolução em praticamente todos os aspectos do primeiro jogo. O conceito de mostrar a evolução do videogame ao passar do tempo, com os respectivos estilos de jogabilidade e visuais, é resgatado e adicionado como parte da trama junto às inúmeras referências e inspirações de jogos que marcaram época. A jogabilidade é divertida e a diversidade de desafios presentes, alternando entre áreas abertas para combate, resolução de enigmas, momentos de plataformas, entre outros permitem que o jogo não seja maçante, e apesar de um início lento, com uma quantidade exagerada de diálogos o enredo é bom e amarra bem todos os elementos.

I originally played the first game, Evoland, back in 2013 and while it was a relatively short game, it stuck with me - mainly for using an interesting gimmick. The game's whole premise was that as you progressed, you would unlock and evolve the world around you. For this reason, new features would be unlocked and the world would change to reflect different RPGs from various eras. It was a brilliant idea that I never found in any other game.

So when I learned that there was an Evoland 2 I had mixed feelings. On the one hand, I wanted to see more of what the first game accomplished. But on the other hand, how does one pull the same trick twice and still remain novel?

Well, the answer is they didn't.

See, in the first game, the devs gave full focus to the gimmick and then slapped into a basic story to tie it all together. This time, however, you could see that they had a full story and then they wrapped the gimmick around that.

In Evoland 2, you don't upgrade your world the same way you do in Evoland. Instead, you travel through time - similar to Chrono Trigger - and each era is represented in an RPG style. So where is the gimmick?

That would be with the different genres they snuck in, and boy did they ever. And yet, at no point did they feel forced. They may have felt out of place, but not forced.

Now while I enjoyed the game, there were a couple of things that bugged me. The first one was that there was no fast travel or escape from the dungeon option. So you spent a lot of time going back and forth to get to the time teleports to shift back and forth. At least, once you unlock the airship, traveling around gets faster.

The second thing that got under my skin was the lack of a sprint feature. It seems trivial, but the amount of times I wanted to get through an area quickly and the character - especially in the Past era - felt like he was moving slowly. It drove me nuts!

There were a couple of other things but overall I enjoyed the game. I would still recommend it, but I am at mixed feelings on whether I prefer the first game or this one.

Evoland 2 est un RPG unique qui rend hommage à toute l’histoire du jeu vidéo, en proposant une aventure où l’on voyage à travers différentes époques avec des styles graphiques allant du pixel art à la 3D. Chaque période apporte sa propre ambiance, rendant le tout très immersif et visuellement plaisant.

Le voyage temporel est captivant : on découvre comment nos actions influencent le futur et chaque époque apporte son lot de surprises. Le gameplay varie énormément, passant d’un RPG classique à des phases de beat’em up, shoot’em up, puzzles et autres mini-jeux, ce qui garde l’expérience constamment fraîche. Les références aux classiques sont légion, et les fans de jeux vidéo trouveront de nombreux clins d’œil amusants. La bande-son accompagne parfaitement chaque époque, renforçant l’immersion et le charme de l’aventure.

Cependant, le rythme peut parfois être inégal : certaines sections sont lentes ou répétitives, et la difficulté varie beaucoup selon les mini-jeux, certains pouvant frustrer. La progression n’est pas toujours claire, ce qui peut créer des moments de confusion où l’on se demande ce qu’il faut faire ensuite.

Evoland 2 reste malgré tout une véritable lettre d’amour aux jeux vidéo, offrant une expérience riche, drôle et variée. Quelques imperfections n’empêchent pas ce titre d’être un incontournable pour les amateurs de RPG et de rétrogaming.
